name: Baking Substitutions
summary: Reliable swaps for buttermilk, baking powder, brown sugar, special flours, butter and eggs, and what each one changes.

rows: 1 cup (240 ml) buttermilk
1 Tbsp (15 ml) lemon juice or white vinegar, plus milk to make 1 cup (240 ml). Let it sit 5 minutes.
Thinner than real buttermilk, but works the same with baking soda.
1 cup (240 ml) buttermilk
¾ cup (180 ml) plain yogurt or sour cream thinned with ¼ cup (60 ml) milk.
Very close; a little richer.
Unsalted butter
Salted butter, with about ¼ tsp less salt per ½ cup (113 g) of butter.
Nearly nothing. Brands vary in how salty they are.

sections.heading: Leaveners

rows: 1 tsp baking powder
¼ tsp baking soda plus ½ tsp cream of tartar.
Single-acting: it all works as soon as it's wet, so bake right after mixing.
1 tsp baking soda
In a pinch, about 3 tsp baking powder.
A different taste and rise, since the recipe's acid is no longer balanced. Fine for pancakes; better to buy baking soda for anything you care about.

blocks: Baking soda and baking powder aren't interchangeable one for one; see [why](guide:baking-ingredients#leaveners). Swapping one type of yeast for another is in the [yeast table](guide:yeast-dough#yeast).

rows: 1 cup (215 g) packed light brown sugar
1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar plus 1 Tbsp (20 g) molasses, mixed well. For dark brown, 2 Tbsp (40 g) molasses.
Nothing noticeable.
1 cup (215 g) brown sugar
1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar.
Crisper, paler cookies with less caramel flavor.
1 cup self-rising flour
1 cup (125 g) all-purpose flour, 1 ½ tsp baking powder and ¼ tsp salt.
Nothing noticeable.
1 cup cake flour
1 cup (125 g) all-purpose flour minus 2 Tbsp, plus 2 Tbsp cornstarch, sifted together.
Slightly less tender than real cake flour.
Bread flour
All-purpose flour, same amount.
Softer, less chewy bread and pizza; the dough may feel wetter.
All-purpose flour
Bread flour, same amount.
Chewier, sometimes tougher; fine in cookies, not ideal in cakes.
Melted butter
A neutral oil, about ¾ the amount.
Moister, softer, less buttery flavor. Works in brownies, quick breads, pancakes and muffins.
Softened or cold butter
Oil doesn't work.
Creaming and flaky doughs need a solid fat. Shortening works for flaky doughs, with less flavor.

sections.heading: Eggs
blocks: Egg swaps work where eggs mostly bind and add moisture: muffins, quick breads, pancakes and many cookies. They don't work where eggs are the structure or the lift: sponge and angel food cakes, custards, meringue, soufflés.

rows: 1 large egg
1 Tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 Tbsp (45 ml) water, left 5 minutes to thicken.
Denser, slightly nutty; good in muffins and quick breads.
1 large egg
¼ cup (60 g) unsweetened applesauce or mashed banana.
Moister and denser, with some flavor of the fruit.
